According to the Maricopa County Department of Public Health, 40 heat-associated fatalities occurred during this time. Additionally, 4 heat-associated fatalities occurred in La Paz County.

High temperatures in Phoenix during this time peaked at 113 degrees on both June 6th and 7th, setting a new record high on the 6th. According to the Maricopa County Department of Public Health, 15 heat-associated fatalities occurred during this time.

The strong winds destroyed some sheds, with the metal roofing becoming entangled around a power pole, knocking power out. Based on the magnitude of the damage observed, wind gusts were estimated to be upwards of 50 mph. No injuries were reported.

As a result, temperatures warmed up well above normal reaching excessive heat conditions. High temperatures climbed at or above 115 degrees each day (6 days) between the 15th-20th, breaking Phoenix's record for consecutive days of 115+ degree temperatures. Temperatures in Phoenix peaked on the 17th at 118 degrees, breaking the record for the date and becoming the hottest temperature for the whole year. According to the Maricopa County Department of Public Health, sixty heat-associated fatalities occurred as a result of this heat wave.

A strong dust devil developed and moved northward in an urbanized sector of Fortuna Foothills just east of Yuma, causing extensive property damage. There were social media images of roofs torn off, roofing tiles blown off, a brick wall collapsing, trees uprooted and massive debris hitting power lines, knocking power out to 2022 customers. The dust devil tracked northward between 10E and 36th Street and South Payson Drive to South Fontage Road near I-8. No injuries were reported.

Continued releases from Painted Rock Dam led to prolonged elevated flows traveling down the Gila River through Yuma County. As a result, numerous downstream unbridged river crossings in Yuma County remained impassable due to flooding. These unbridged crossings remained closed through the month of May. According to local media reports, Yuma County Public Works reported that 14 unbridged crossings, which include Roll Road (paved) and 13 dirt roads, sustained damage due to the prolonged elevated flows in the river.

Imperial Dam Road between the Walker and Howard Gates at the Yuma Proving Ground Naval Base was closed for several days due to major road erosion from flash flooding. Flood timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
